brief: BofA expects September payrolls to rise by a below-consensus 60k (private 50k), down from 162k in August, because August's unusually favorable seasonal adjustment should reverse in September; underlying job growth remains resilient above 100k, with hiring broadening across construction, manufacturing, and professional/business services. The unemployment rate should hold at 4.1% as participation stays at 61.6%, though payback in household employment (which surged 569k in August) could push it to 4.2%. Haitian TPS visa revocations (~200k workers) are a gradual headwind, not a shock. BofA argues the labor market's true breakeven pace of job growth may be above its 20k/month estimate given immigration constraints, but the 3-month average of 80k still clears that bar. Because growth is resilient and inflation is sticky, BofA maintains an out-of-consensus call for the Fed to hike twice more (25bp each) in October and December; it expects September's jobs report to matter less for that decision than September CPI. Separately, rising net interest costs (3.3% of GDP, a record) suggest Treasury yields may need to rise further before fiscal discipline returns, while surging household balance sheets (assets now above 10x liabilities) cushion consumer spending against an equity pullback.
